 HOOPS San Miguel Beermen vs Barangay Ginebra PBA Governors’ Cup Game 5 
 PBA Beeracle comeback San Miguel 0-2 series deficit 
 PBA Season 50 Governors’ Cup quarterfinals semifinals TNT 
 San Miguel on cusp of ‘Beeracle’
 Mark Escarlote · 9 November 2026 · 4:36 AM PHT · 3 MIN READ 
 PBA
 Text size A− Reset A+ Save San Miguel Beer is no stranger to pulling off miraculous comebacks from a series deficit.
 In fact, the Beermen hold the distinction as the only team in Philippine Basketball Association (PBA) history to recover from a deep 0-3 hole in a best-of-seven series, in a feat popularly known as the “Beeracle” comeback from a decade ago.
 The league’s winningest franchise is again on the cusp of another epic reversal.
 Also read UE hero earns scribes’ approval 
 It erased a 0-2 best-of-five quarterfinals series deficit against Barangay Ginebra and forcing a do-or-die in the PBA Season 50 Governors’ Cup on Tuesday at the Ynares Center-Antipolo.
 Also read
 HOOPS AVERTING DISASTER
 Kings go for jugular; Beermen stay defiant
 Mark Escarlote · 3 November 2026 
 However, even with momentum — and history — on their side, San Miguel head coach Leo Austria downplayed the ‘Beeracle’ angle and would rather focus on just getting the job done.
 “We will not exaggerate the situation. We just have to play our game. We just want to focus on what we’re doing,” Austria said.
 Back in the 2016 Philippine Cup, San Miguel also had its back against the wall after three games before winning the last four matches to steal the series from Alaska and complete a feat never before accomplished in Asia’s first play-for-pay league.
 The Beermen equalized in Game 4, coming back from 17 points down with a massive 46-point third-quarter burst for a come-from-behind, 108-102, victory last Friday at the Smart Araneta Coliseum. 
 Also read UAAP slaps Alas with 2-game ban 
 San Miguel turned the tables around after dropping the first two games.
 In the equalizer, the Beermen limited the Kings to just 18 points in the third quarter. They also made life difficult for RJ Abarrientos as the Ginebra guard went 2-of-13 from the field for just seven points and without a single assist.
 “One of the game plans is to limit Abarrientos, which I think materialized. He scored only seven points,” Austria said.
 Stephen Holt had it worse with San Miguel’s stingy defense.
 Also read
 HOOPS Closing time?
 Kings smell blood, seek to send Beermen packing
 Mark Escarlote · 6 November 2026 
 “Holt is usually averaging in double figures but now he only got three points. And Jeremiah Gray, only six points. I think our defense said a lot in this game,” the 11-time champion coach added.
 George King, ageless Chris Ross, CJ Perez and Don Trollano shouldered much of the scoring as center June Mar Fajardo struggled to find his form on offense.
 “And when it comes to offense, our team is very talented. But if we play as a team, I think we will be having good results,” Austria said.
 The winner of the rubbermatch takes on defending champion TNT in the best-of-five semifinals starting 4 December.
